examples.question_text:
The colours of cars passing a school were recorded:
Red, Blue, White, Blue, Red, White, Blue, Red, Blue.
Construct a frequency table and check its total.
examples.solution_text:
List each colour and count how often it appears.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Car colour}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline\text{Red}&3\\\text{Blue}&4\\\text{White}&2\end{array}$
Check: $3+4+2=9$, matching the nine recorded cars.

examples.question_text:
These scores were recorded:
$2,0,3,1,2,3,0,2,1,3,2,1$.
Construct a frequency table and check that its total equals the number of scores.
examples.solution_text:
List the scores in increasing order, then count each score.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Score}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline0&2\\1&3\\2&4\\3&3\end{array}$
A score of $0$ is a recorded result, so count it too.
Check: $2+3+4+3=12$, matching the twelve scores.

examples.question_text:
A student records car colours using the categories Red, Blue, White and Green.
The observations are:
White, Red, Blue, White, Blue, White, Red, Blue, White, Blue.
Construct a frequency table with a row for every named category and check its total.
examples.solution_text:
Count each named category. Keep Green in the table even though no green cars were recorded.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Car colour}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline\text{Red}&2\\\text{Blue}&4\\\text{White}&4\\\text{Green}&0\end{array}$
Green has frequency $0$.
Check: $2+4+4+0=10$, matching the ten observations.

coverage.summary: Added three worked examples covering categorical counts, numerical counts and named categories with zero frequency. Each uses the supplied booklet's counting-and-total-check method with different data and Stage 3 terminology. Questions and solutions are separate; editable solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. No continuation gutters or diagrams are needed. Accepted assessments were used only to classify methods and were neither changed nor re-audited.

examples.derivation: Independent count: Red occurs 3 times, Blue 4 times and White 2 times. The frequencies total 3+4+2=9, matching all nine observations. This adapts the categorical frequency-table example at source lines 128–155.

Independent count: score 0 occurs twice, score 1 three times, score 2 four times and score 3 three times. The frequencies total 2+3+4+3=12. Increasing score order and counting recorded zeros follow Foundation question 1(a), including attached images image4.png and image5.png.

Independent count: Red occurs twice, Blue four times, White four times and Green zero times. Every explicitly named category is retained. The frequencies total 2+4+4+0=10. The source worked example at lines 128–152 likewise retains Green with zero frequency.

review.summary: All 21 exact assessment locators are mapped correctly, with coverage for categorical counting, numerical counting and retaining absent named categories. All three examples follow supplied source methods, use different observations and remain within Stage 3 scope. No existing examples require preservation. Separate question and solution fields, single-dollar mathematics and inherited blue solution styling comply. No continuation gutters or additional diagrams are needed. No syllabus exception is required. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited.
